brief: A three-storey tower: drawers on the bottom storey and open bins on the top storey.

requirements.evidence: Full hex bases stacked at (0,0) on levels 0, 1 and 2, with snap connectors between storeys.

A half base (half-w) at (1,0,0) on level 0 is joined to the tower by a snap and a joint bolt, and carries one slide drawer (drawer:0#1,0#cut) on its cut face. Only one drawer is placed; the notch-frame spot I tried was removed because no drawer would attach to it.

requirements.requirement: Open bins on the top storey
requirements.evidence: A full-depth open bin (bin:0,0,2~hex-bin-full) sits in the top cell at level 2. Only one bin is placed.

finish.summary: The build is a three-storey tower. Level 0 has a slide drawer on a half base, level 2 has an open full-depth bin, and level 1 is a connecting base. check_build reports no rule errors and meshClash is clear. The build is minimal (one drawer, one bin), and I did not add more storage cells.

M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
